newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian minister Di Rupo keeps two lives separate.
newsitem.headline: Belgian minister Di Rupo keeps two lives separate.

text.p: Belgium's bow-tie wearing Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo, a discreet homosexual facing paedophilia allegations, has risen to the political heights by successfully keeping his private and public lives apart.

In vigorously denying the allegations which could spell a swift end to his sparkling career, Di Rupo has been forced openly to defend his unconventional lifestyle - no secret to politicians and journalists - for the first time.

Di Rupo, 45, told reporters he was the victim of confusion between events in his private life - involving consenting and responsible adults - "which do nobody any harm" and "disgusting, outrageous acts which people want to attribute to me."
In Humo current events magazine he said, "All my life I have been confronted with all sorts of rumours, but fortunately they have never influenced my political career."
The child sex allegations come at a time when Belgium is highly sensitised, after the discovery in August of a paedophile and murder scandal traumatised the small catholic country.
Ironically, Di Rupo has won the limelight recently by leading a quest for a ban on material featuring sexual abuse or child pornography on the Internet.
Behind Di Rupo's affable manner and trademark wide grin, though, lies a strong-willed and ambitious politician.

As economics minister his beaming portrait recently adorned the government's 'Invest in Belgium' site on the Worldwide Web but it was removed after a storm of public criticism that he was using a government publication to promote himself.

Di Rupo says he found his political vocation during a "passionate" youth when he discovered the world and its injustices. In his words, he longed to change it, to make society "more harmonious and just".
One of seven children born in a Belgian ghetto of Italian immigrants, Di Rupo lost his father when he was a year old and was placed with an impoverished Belgium family.
Neighbours helped pay for him to study physics and Di Rupo was an academic until he entered parliament for the francophone socialist PS party in 1987.
After a spell as a member of the European Parliament, he took up his first government post at the end of 1992 as minister of community affairs in the francophone community government.
His career moved into top gear in January 1994 when three federal PS ministers lost their jobs over a bribes-for-arms orders scandal and Di Rupo was put forward for a cabinet post.
He was made one of four deputy prime ministers, in charge of transport and public companies.

Di Rupo shook off initial doubts about his ability to operate at the highest political level in Belgium at a relatively young age, was re-elected in 1995 and strengthened his position both in his own party and in the government.
After the election his ministerial portfolios were swapped for economy and telecommunications.
Also facing allegations of under-age sex is the French Community's minister for higher education, Jean-Pierre Grafe (pronounced Graffay).
Like Di Rupo he strongly denies the allegations.
